component.name: Moji Plus
component.summary: Clean Markdown viewer and editor, based on Moji

description.p: Moji+ opens, previews, edits, and exports Markdown files in a compact desktop workspace.
It is a derivative of Moji by Alex Ishida (https://github.com/alexishida/Moji), distributed under the MIT License, and keeps receiving the changes made to the original project.
It supports split preview and editing, outline navigation, search and replace, localized UI, and export to PDF, HTML, and PNG.

ul.li: Plain text files (.txt) open as written, and more Markdown extensions are recognised (.mdown, .mkd, .mkdn, .markdn, .mdx).
Ticking a task list checkbox in the preview updates the document.
Windows: updating or uninstalling no longer fails with "cannot be closed" on PCs that block programs in the temporary folder.
Fixes a crash at launch on macOS in version 1.5.0.
Front matter is shown as a properties panel instead of a YAML code block, also in exports.
New, Close and Save buttons in the toolbar; Save is only enabled when there are changes.
Capsule-shaped buttons, Export in its own group, and the sidebar button on the sidebar.
A setting to always show the tab bar, a larger tab close button and an accent-coloured unsaved mark.
On macOS the menu bar and the Dock show the name as Moji+.
The Settings window looks like the settings of current macOS apps.
The sidebar slides in and out, and the selection of the view switch and of the tabs slides between items.
Saving a new document suggests a file name based on its content.
A minimal preview style with larger headings, and wide tables that fit the exported page.
Local images inside picture elements, as GitHub READMEs use, now show in the preview.
The DMG and the Windows installer have their own icon.
Windows and Linux get the same interface and layout as macOS: full-height sidebar, single-row toolbar, Safari-style tabs and the same colors.
The app menu opens from a button in the top-left corner, and the native window controls sit at the right of the toolbar.
New icon, and the app is now written Moji+ in its interface.
Native menus, context menus and alerts; Settings opens in its own window and Export as a sheet over the document.
On macOS, the interface follows Apple's Human Interface Guidelines: a full-height translucent sidebar, a single-row toolbar, the system font, colors and accent color.
Visible keyboard focus, arrow-key navigation in the outline, and support for reduced motion and increased contrast.
Open documents changed or removed by other applications are detected, and saving never overwrites such a change without asking.
The last session reopens: tabs in order, unsaved changes to files, view mode, outline, full width, maximized window and each document's reading position.
Undoing every edit clears the unsaved-changes mark.
Closing an untitled document with content asks whether to save it.
The status bar token count is shown as an estimate.
Select All in the preview selects only the document.
Local images in HTML img tags load in the preview and in exports.
The About panel scrolls in small windows.
macOS now checks for a newer Moji Plus, like Windows and Linux.
On Windows and Linux, scrollbars stay hidden until you scroll or hover over them, like on macOS.
PDF export prints white page margins instead of dark ones.

description.p: First Moji Plus release, based on Moji 1.0.7.

ul.li: Light and dark themes for the whole app, following the OS theme by default.
YAML front matter rendered as a highlighted code block in the preview and exports.
No native title bar: the top bar fills the top of the window with the native window controls.
Own name, icon, settings directory, and releases, so it installs next to the original Moji.
